doc: Under the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), Iran was restricted to a total enriched uranium stockpile of no more than 300 kg of up to 3.67% enriched uranium hexafluoride for 15 years, equivalent to 202.8 kg. Iran continued enrichment after the deal but did not enrich above 3.67% in 2016. By January 2020, a senior Iranian official claimed the stockpile had reached 1,200 kg, more than doubling in three months, while a separate report indicated a stockpile of around 2,105 kg of enriched uranium. The IAEA found approximately 550 kg of uranium hexafluoride enriched to less than 4.5% as of late 2019; if further enriched, this quantity could yield more than 30 kg of weapons-grade uranium, enough for one fission bomb.
